tonight.headline: Waivers cleared: the tight end and the defence are free now, and one claim is worth making tonight
body: Bad news first. You are 0–4, your tight-end slot still projects 0.0 with Waller on bye, the Ravens' defence is still your lowest number at 4.9, and Tuten is still on the bench behind Gordon. As set you project 101.9 against 123.3 and ESPN gives you 39%. Barkley has no ruling yet.

Everything Tuesday's brief was waiting for cleared at 01:00: Strange, Loveland, Hockenson, the Jaguars and the Cowboys are all free agents this morning. Add Strange for Waller and the Jaguars for the Ravens today. One thing is new: George Pickens was dropped overnight and is on waivers until 01:00 on Thursday. That is the one claim I would put in. With all of it you project about 118.

case.label: Their side
case.body: Nacua 21.7, Goff 18.5, Kyren Williams 17.9, Jeremiyah Love 15.1 after tweaking his other ankle (status depends on practice; DraftKings Network lists him 'TBD'), Tee Higgins 14.3 and day-to-day (AP, 7 Oct: he and Chase 'may miss' Miami), Watson 13.8, Kittle 13.7. Their defence is still Kansas City's, on bye at 0.0.

case.label: Your side once it is set
case.body: Taylor 19.0, Lawrence 18.1, Wilson 14.6, Tuten 14.0, Tate 13.6, Golden 12.8, Strange 9.7, Myers 8.7 and the Jaguars 7.7: 118.2. Pickens, if the claim lands, would be a coin flip with Golden for the flex at 13.3.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Barkley practising in full, on your side. Love or Higgins sitting, on theirs.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Free now · anyone can take him · Strange locks Sun 07:30 Mexico City
doFirst.title: Add Strange for Waller, now
doFirst.subtitle: Your tight-end slot projects 0.0. Strange, Loveland and Hockenson all cleared waivers and are free. Take Strange; if he is gone, Loveland, then Hockenson.

case.label: The hole
case.body: Waller is on bye and he is your only tight end. Free this morning and within a point of each other: T.J. Hockenson 10.4, Brenton Strange 9.7, Colston Loveland 9.7, Mark Andrews 9.6. They are free agents now, so adding them costs no priority. It also means any of nine other managers can take them before you do.

case.label: Why Strange first
case.body: 7 catches on 8 targets for 95 on 87% of the snaps in Week 4 (archive; PlayerProfiler). Tuesday's question was whether an injury explained it, and today's research says no: Brian Thomas Jr., Travis Hunter and Jakobi Meyers all played and none is on Jacksonville's injury list. He is the offence's second receiving option behind Parker Washington, signed a three-year extension in the offseason, and led all tight ends in yards per route last week at 4.5 (SI, 5 Oct). Targets 3, 2, 5, 8.

case.label: Why not the others
case.body: Loveland: a team-high 9 targets from Tyson Bagent, who starts again, and no bye until Week 10; the same projection, and one game of volume. He is the fallback. Hockenson has the highest number, but his 13 targets came with Jefferson out, Jefferson may play, and Minnesota are off in Week 6, which empties the slot again in five days. Andrews: Lamar Jackson still has 'only an outside chance' and Tyler Huntley is 'trending toward starting' (CBS, 6 Oct).

case.label: The drop, and the rule it bends
case.body: Waller. Neither clause of his open thesis has tripped, and you added him on 3 Oct, so both the thesis rule and the churn rule say leave him. This is the exception and I am saying so: Wilson, Kamara, Gordon, Barkley and Rice each have an injured teammate and can't be named, the other seats are starters, and a tight end on bye is a slot at zero. Week 4 showed what he is: 53% of the snaps and a 15.4% target share, with 'other tight ends remained involved' (FTN, 5 Oct). ESPN's season number has him at 92.2 against Strange's 127.9.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: Jacksonville are off in Week 7, so Strange brings a bye of his own in two weeks. Philadelphia allow the fifth-fewest points to tight ends in this scoring. And 95 yards matched his previous three games combined.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: The tight end you add scores less on Sunday than another of the three who was still free when you added (archive). For the drop: Waller outscores him in two of Weeks 6 to 8.

doFirst.title: Swap the Ravens' defence for the Jaguars', free
doFirst.subtitle: 4.9 against 7.7. Lamar Jackson still has 'only an outside chance'; Jacksonville get an Eagles offence without Bigsby, Smith, Goedert or Lane Johnson, and probably without Barkley.

case.label: The gap
case.body: The Ravens project 4.9, the lowest number in your lineup. Free defences this morning: Cowboys 8.4, Jets 7.9, Commanders 7.8, Jaguars 7.7, Steelers 7.4. The gap to Jacksonville is 2.8, outside the coin-flip line, which is the bar the strategy sets for a streaming move. They are free agents now, so adding them costs no priority.

case.label: Why Jacksonville
case.body: Philadelphia put Tank Bigsby on injured reserve on Tuesday evening, Lane Johnson retired the same day, DeVonta Smith is out for multiple weeks, Dallas Goedert missed Week 4, and Barkley has no ruling. Hurts was pressured on 57.6% of his dropbacks last week (Inquirer, 6 Oct). The line has moved to Jacksonville −6.5 with a total of 42.5. NBC ranks the Jaguars 1st for the week and RotoWire 3rd; FantasyPros has them 9th.

case.label: The Cowboys are a coin flip above them
case.body: Dallas project 8.4, 0.7 higher, as 8.5-point favourites at home to an undrafted rookie quarterback on Thursday; FantasyPros ranks them 1st, RotoWire 4th, NBC 9th. So the lists split exactly the other way. I stay with Jacksonville on Philadelphia's injury list, which is reporting I can point to; FantasyPros itself notes Dallas are last among defences in fantasy scoring and NBC that they allow 28 a game. Either is far better than 4.9. Dallas lock on Thursday at 18:15.

case.label: Baltimore's side
case.body: Atlanta are favoured by 2.5 to 3 after the line opened at Baltimore −6. Marlon Humphrey (calf) and Trey Hendrickson (finger) have no return dates. Dropping an 80%-owned defence needs a reason on the record, and that is it. FantasyPros ranks the Ravens 28th this week.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: Jacksonville's corners Montaric Brown and Christian Braswell and safeties Eric Murray and Caleb Ransaw are all listed questionable (CBS, 4–5 Oct). Jacksonville are off in Week 7, so this is a one- or two-week seat.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: The Ravens outscore the Jaguars in Week 5 (archive), or Barkley and Smith both play.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Waivers clear Thu 01:00 Mexico City · he plays Thu 18:15
doFirst.title: Put in a claim for George Pickens
doFirst.subtitle: Drop Josh Downs. KEI returns cut a 99%-rostered receiver for Romeo Doubs at 02:07. You are 7th of ten; a claim that fails costs nothing.

case.label: The player
case.body: Healthy and playing 83% of Dallas's snaps as the second receiver (RotoWire). 18 catches for 225 on 28 targets in four games and no touchdown yet; targets 6, 8, 11, 3 (archive). The 3 came in a game where CeeDee Lamb drew 21 of Dak Prescott's 45 attempts, and he still had catches of 53 and 22 yards. Dallas are 8.5-point favourites on Thursday with a total of 47.5. ESPN projects 13.3 this week and 176.6 for the season.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Josh Downs: 12.1 this week and 134.6 for the season, the lowest receiver number on your roster. His thesis closed WRONG on Sunday on 4 targets with Pierce, Allen and Slayton all missing. He is 82% owned, so this disagrees with the market on the record: the reason is that Pickens is the same kind of player with a better number, 42 points better over the season by ESPN's count. Downs is not on the screen's exposure list.

case.label: Why this is the one to spend priority on
case.body: The strategy allows a claim only for a player who would start at once. Pickens would: 13.3 is above Golden's 12.8 and Downs's 12.1 for the flex. That is a coin flip this week and I am not writing a lineup thesis on it. The case is the season number and the snap share. The price is three places, 7th to 10th, in an order that never resets, and only if the claim wins. Six managers are ahead of you, so it probably doesn't.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: He is the second option behind a receiver who took 47% of the targets last week, and your record on adds is poor. If it lands, free agents still cost nothing, but any later claim is made from last place. Neither the waiver tool nor the wire screen surfaced him: both measure rising usage, and a just-dropped starter doesn't rise. This card is my judgement, not the tool's.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Downs outscores Pickens in two of Weeks 5 to 7 (archive), or Pickens draws fewer than six targets in two of those three games.

doFirst.title: Start Tuten in the RB slot, not Gordon
doFirst.subtitle: Still not done: Gordon is in Barkley's slot. The projection has Tuten 3.1 higher, 14.0 to 10.9, and he kicks off first.

case.label: What the check says
case.body: lineup_check.py: start Tuten over Gordon, PROJECTION, 3.1 points. It is the only change outside the coin-flip line. As set you project 101.9; the projection lineup is 105.7.

case.label: Why Tuten
case.body: 17 of Jacksonville's 23 backfield carries on Sunday and two touchdowns called back for penalties (archive; SI, 5 Oct). Jacksonville are 6.5-point favourites. He is not on Jacksonville's injury list after his brief exit on Sunday.

case.label: Why not Gordon
case.body: 9 carries for 100 on Sunday, more than half of it on one 53-yard run, after 17 carries the week before with Wright out. Nobody in Miami has named a starter: Hafley's Monday transcript doesn't mention either back. Miami are 7-point underdogs and ran 38 plays last week. You spent a claim on him and a start would count toward that thesis; that isn't a reason to give up three points.

case.label: The flex is a coin flip
case.body: Downs is in the flex at 12.1 and the projection prefers Golden at 12.8. That is 0.7, so take Golden and write nothing down. If the Pickens claim lands, Downs is gone anyway and Thursday's check decides between Pickens and Golden.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Gordon outscores Tuten on Sunday (archive).

waiverAnalysis.summary: Eleven names clear the tool's bar, ten of them the same as Tuesday, and at running back and receiver the bar is an artefact: it measures them against Barkley and Rice, whose last week was an injury exit each. Four weeks of data. The only question research turns into a move is at tight end, where the tool doesn't see that Waller is on bye; that is the first card. The tool did not print George Pickens, who is the third card: it looks for rising usage, and he was dropped, not rising.

rising.name: Keaton Mitchell
rising.roleReason: A three-man rotation by design with Omarion Hampton healthy: Mitchell led at 36.6% of the snaps in Week 4, 10 carries and 6 targets, with Hampton and Vidal at 25-plus snaps each (FTN, 5 Oct). Jim Harbaugh says it 'is best for our team'. Yahoo's number two add. The Chargers are off in Week 7.
rising.action: WATCH — a committee third; the trigger is Hampton missing a game
rising.sources: FTN · Yahoo · Last Word on Sports

rising.name: Brian Robinson Jr.
rising.roleReason: Bijan Robinson is healthy and had 20 touches to Brian Robinson's 15. Three touchdowns came in a 45–24 win; FTN (6 Oct) calls him a blowout beneficiary with fewer touches expected in close games. Double-digit carries three weeks running: a real second role behind a healthy starter.
rising.action: WATCH — touchdowns and game script behind a healthy starter

rising.name: MarShawn Lloyd
rising.roleReason: 7 carries for 13 and 5 catches for 36; Kaleb Johnson ran 8 times for 42 and fumbled at the goal line. LaFleur has warned that ball security decides playing time. Josh Jacobs is still on the exempt list with no ruling. You dropped him for Gordon.
rising.action: WATCH — volume at 1.9 yards a carry in a backfield nobody has won

rising.name: Mike Washington Jr.
rising.roleReason: Ashton Jeanty's handcuff: 10 touches for 17 yards while Jeanty had 21 (CBS, 4 Oct). Nothing changed.
rising.action: WATCH — nothing unless Jeanty is hurt

rising.name: Devaughn Vele
rising.roleReason: 6 catches on 9 targets for 54 and a touchdown while Shough threw 48 times from behind; CBS calls him a high-volume second receiver. Jordyn Tyson is not expected before Week 7 and Week 9 is likelier (Yahoo). The steadiest role on this list.
rising.action: WATCH — a real role, as a sixth receiver; free now, but there is no seat

rising.name: Khalil Shakir
rising.roleReason: 7 catches on 8 targets for 82 in the game DJ Moore left with an aggravated AC joint; Moore has no practice status yet and Keon Coleman is the Bill the columns prefer for the extra targets.

rising.name: Tyquan Thornton
rising.roleReason: Dislocated his left ankle on Sunday after 5 catches for 111 and two touchdowns; surgery this week, out 12 to 16 weeks (Rapoport, 5 Oct).
rising.action: WATCH — off the list: out until at least January
rising.sources: A to Z Sports · PFT · FTN

rising.name: Keon Coleman
rising.roleReason: 6 catches on 7 targets for 116 and a touchdown on 78% of the snaps after DJ Moore left with an aggravated AC joint; 12 for 179 in the two games Moore left early (FTN). Moore is 'not considered long-term' and has no practice status yet, so the role is exactly as long as his absence.
rising.action: WATCH — a role that exists only while Moore is out; Buffalo's first report comes late in the week

rising.name: T.J. Hockenson
rising.roleReason: A 35% target share with Jefferson out. Jefferson is questionable and expected to 'push to play' (Goessling, 6 Oct); Minnesota are off in Week 6.
rising.action: WATCH — last of the three tight ends for Waller's slot; see the first card

rising.name: Michael Mayer
rising.roleReason: 8 catches for 82 on 10 targets beside a healthy Brock Bowers, who had 11. FTN (6 Oct, 21:33 ET) gives two reasons: Jalen Nailor's concussion, and Klint Kubiak wanting both tight ends involved. The second is a scheme reason, which is more durable than the first.
rising.action: WATCH — behind the three in the first card; a second tight end on his own team

rising.name: Brenton Strange
rising.roleReason: 8 targets, 95 yards and 87% of the snaps with every Jacksonville pass-catcher healthy, so no injury explains it. He is the second receiving option behind Parker Washington and led tight ends in yards per route last week at 4.5 (SI, 5 Oct). Targets 3, 2, 5, 8.
rising.action: ADD — free as of this morning; first in the first card's order, for Waller
